diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement lines 31–35 fixes x^- in the incoming d-dimensional mode and R(t,x) in the outgoing d-dimensional mode. The diagram defines z_delta^- = phi^-(tau_delta;tau,x^-+delta x^-) and restricts to delta tau > 0, hence t0=tau_delta. By the selected-root hypothesis, g(tau_delta,z_delta^-)=0; the nominal guard label is g(tau,x^-)=0. The definition supplier requires each reset to land in the outgoing domain at the unchanged event time. Both vertical reset arrows have that exact domain/codomain interpretation.

The upper horizontal arrow is the incoming flow from time tau to tau_delta, as used in proof 1.1 and 2.1. The lower arrow is nominal outgoing flow from R(tau,x^-) to x^+(t0), exactly the delta tau >= 0 branch in step 2.1. The right reset ends at the outgoing right limit R(tau_delta,z_delta^-)=x_delta^+(t0). The dashed upward arrow is explicitly defined as perturbed minus nominal state at the same t0 and is not asserted to be a flow. Heights are explicitly schematic, avoiding any asserted ordering of d-dimensional states.

Proof 1.1 gives delta tau = -D_x g delta x^- / kappa + o(norm delta x^-), with kappa = partial_t g + D_x g f^- nonzero. Step 2.1 gives reset contribution D_x R delta x^- + (D_x R f^- + partial_t R) delta tau, minus nominal outgoing advance f^+ delta tau. Substitution changes the sign to the stated (f^+ - D_x R f^- - partial_t R)D_x g/kappa. For delta tau < 0 the perturbed outgoing branch instead advances to tau, as retained in the caption and proof.

D_x R is d by d; f^+, D_x R f^-, and partial_t R are d-columns; D_x g is a 1 by d row; kappa is scalar. The correction is consequently d by d. No commutativity or extra trajectory-existence claim is introduced. The existing rigorous proof, including both shift signs, is unchanged and independent of the figure.
